mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.2% signals an aggressive monetary easing cycle, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 8.0% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger risk-off sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.0% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a contraction in aggregate demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-crisis recovery regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 index points signals ongoing supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances during the post-crisis recovery period when INDPRO is below 90.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 320,000 million dollars signals strong consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS exceeds 320,000 million dollars, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening cycle that increases the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for 2 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 215.0 index points indicate a stagflationary environment, which triggers negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines and CPIAUCSL exceeds 215.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the high-unemployment regime, a decline in payroll employment below 132,000 thousand persons signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS falls below 132,000 thousand persons in the high-unemployment regime, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.
